claims.text: Sync status compares the manifests in Git with the live objects; it does not check whether an image a manifest names exists in the registry, so a missing image shows only in health status.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Sync Status / Resource Health; output line 2 'staging: Synced, Progressing' @ stage-3

claims.text: kubectl rollout undo makes the Deployment's previous revision current again and changes only the live object, not the manifest in Git; kubectl prints 'deployment.apps/api rolled back' after a PodSecurity Warning line that does not stop it.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Deployments > Rolling Back a Deployment; kubectl rollout undo; output line 8 @ stage-3

claims.text: With self-heal on, after kubectl rollout undo the Deployment names 1.0.0 right after, then Argo CD applies the bad tag from Git again within the script's wait (up to 120 checks, a second apart).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy > Automatic Self-Healing; gitops-revert.sh:38-41 and output lines 9-10 @ stage-3

claims.text: Argo CD can roll an Application back to a revision from its sync history, but rollback cannot be performed against an Application with automated sync enabled.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Automated Sync Policy ('Rollback cannot be performed against an application with automated sync enabled'); argocd app rollback reference

claims.text: git revert adds a new commit whose changes undo an earlier commit, leaving both in the history; --no-edit keeps the default message 'Revert "<subject>"' without an editor; -C <dir> runs git in that folder; -c user.name=... sets the author for that command.
claims.source_hint: git docs: git-revert (--no-edit); git (-C, -c options); output line 14 @ stage-3

claims.text: Once the revert commit is pushed, automated sync applies it like any deploy: the Application becomes Synced, Healthy and only 1.0.0 Pods run.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy; gitops-revert.sh:47-56 and output lines 12-13 @ stage-3

claims.text: A revert changes manifests in Git only; migrations a hook already applied stay in the database, so going back past a schema change needs the older api to work with the newer schema.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 5; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/gitops/config-repo/envs/staging/migrate-hook.yaml (hook runs migrations during sync)

claims.text: Force-pushing a reset branch moves the server's branch back, dropping later commits; Argo CD follows it. A teammate whose clone holds the removed commit pushes a new one on top: the server's branch is an ancestor of theirs, so the plain push is accepted (fast-forward) and brings the bad tag back.
claims.source_hint: git docs: git-push (fast-forward), git-reset; Argo CD docs: Tracking and Deployment Strategies (targetRevision main)

claims.text: gitops-revert.sh: 9-10 good (1.0.0), bad (sha- zeros); 25-26 edit api.yaml tag, commit, push; 27-29 refresh, wait; 30 wait ErrImagePull; 31 api_images (count, tag, ready, reason); 38 undo; 40 ≤120 checks 1 s apart; 48 revert HEAD; 49 keep its id; 50-51 push; 52-55 wait; 56 api_images; 57 log -n 3.
Prefer a revert commit over reset and force-push when the branch is shared and its log is the deploy history; the history then keeps both the mistake and its fix.

When the older api does not work with the newer schema, prefer going forward over a revert: commit the tag of an image that fixes the bug and works with the new schema, and let automated sync deploy it.
